subject: Exec update: Hosted overload protection (circuit breakers + load shedding) — canary results + rollout plan
related_links: Grafana: Overload Protection / Hosted API (internal dashboard)
body:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 5, 2026 at 8:12 AM PT
Subject: Exec update: Hosted overload protection (circuit breakers + load shedding) — canary results + rollout plan

Team — quick exec-level update on Hosted overload protection rollout (circuit breakers + deterministic load shedding across gateway → routing/control plane → runtime).

TL;DR
- Canary in us-east has been stable since 12/18 with meaningful reduction in overload-driven incidents and a much cleaner customer experience under spikes (429/503 w/ Retry-After vs ambiguous timeouts).
- We fixed the main canary risk (breaker flapping) last week and validated via game-day-style drills + perf canary.
- Request: approval to expand from us-east canary to 2 additional regions in staged rollout starting week of 1/13, keeping per-(model, region) feature flags + fast rollback.

What we shipped (currently enabled in canary scope)
- Edge admission control hook (tier/route classification, early shed where possible)
- Routing breaker state (per model/region/tier), hysteresis + cooldown
- Runtime bounded queues + deterministic shed points (prefill boundary + scheduling boundary)
- Standardized overload error payload + headers:
  - 429 for “over capacity / try later” cases where client action is to back off
  - 503 for “service unavailable” cases tied to regional brownout / breaker open
  - Retry-After: provided on all overload-protected responses
  - Redwood error codes are consistent across REST + OpenAI-compat endpoints

Canary scope
- Region: us-east
- Models: 2 high-volume Hosted models (one chat, one embeddings)
- Tenants: ~6% of Hosted traffic, skewed toward higher-throughput PLG customers (no Dedicated pools)

Canary results (12/18–01/04)
1) Incident volume / severity
- Overload-related Sev1/Sev2 incidents: down 60–70% in us-east vs prior 4-week baseline (apples-to-apples: spike windows).
- “Cascading failure” pattern (queue blowups → tail latency collapse → gateway timeouts): not observed in the canary window.

2) Latency and stability
- p99 latency during step-function spikes improved materially (fewer runaway tails); median unchanged.
- Control plane remained responsive during spikes (routing did not degrade into timeouts).

3) Error semantics (customer experience)
- During overload windows, ambiguous 5xx timeouts decreased sharply.
- The majority of shed responses were 429 with Retry-After (client actionable); 503 reserved for breaker-open / regional protection.
- We did see a small increase in 429 counts in the canary population (expected), but with better client outcomes (fewer long-hanging requests).

4) Retries / storm risk
- No platform-wide retry storm observed; however, we caught one client pattern in support where the customer retried immediately without jitter.
- SDK improvements are in flight to make safe backoff harder to get wrong (and docs are being updated).

Key risk we hit + mitigation
- Breaker flapping: discovered in early canary (transitions were too sensitive to fast-moving queue depth signals under burst).
- Mitigation: increased cooldown + added hysteresis logic + regression test.
- Status: fixed and deployed (ref: redwood/pr-18519). Canary has remained stable since.

Remaining risks before full deployment
1) Client retry behavior (external)
- Even with Retry-After, some clients will ignore it.
- Plan: ship SDK surfaces + docs (DevEx) and add support macros; also consider response header guidance expansion (e.g., explicit “do not retry streaming reconnects immediately”).

2) Metric/label cardinality and alert noise
- Current dashboards look good, but we need another round of alert tuning once we expand beyond us-east.
- Oncall alignment: load shedding must not page as “internal failure” when behaving as designed; SLO tooling changes are in progress.

3) Dedicated alignment
- Dedicated customers have different expectations re: capacity predictability. We are keeping Hosted and Dedicated behavior aligned where it makes sense (error semantics), while avoiding surprise shedding where Dedicated contractually implies reserved throughput.
- Lauren: we should confirm the “Dedicated-only” path remains unchanged during Hosted rollout.

Rollout plan (proposal)
- Week of 1/13: expand feature flags to us-west + eu-west for same 2 models, keep 5–10% traffic caps.
- Week of 1/20: broaden model coverage in those regions; increase caps as metrics hold.
- Week of 1/27: global expansion gated by: shed rate, p99, breaker open duration, and customer ticket volume.
- Rollback: per region/model flag (instant), plus admin toggle for emergency disable in a region.

Ask / decision
- If you’re aligned, I’ll green-light the next phase per above and we’ll send a company-wide note with what to watch + where to report issues.

Attachments
- overload-protection-exec-update-2026-01-05.pdf
- us-east-canary-metrics-2026-01-04.png

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference


---

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 5, 2026 at 8:41 AM PT
Subject: Re: Exec update: Hosted overload protection (circuit breakers + load shedding) — canary results + rollout plan

Thanks Sean — this is the kind of “fail clearly vs fail mysteriously” improvement we’ve needed.

I’m aligned with expanding to us-west + eu-west with caps + fast rollback.

Two asks from product side:
1) Can we add a short internal note we can share with Support/CS on how to explain the *increase in 429s* without it sounding like regression (i.e., “now you’re seeing the protective behavior instead of timeouts”)?
2) Let’s keep an eye on OpenAI-compat clients in particular (we’ve had past sensitivity around error shapes).

-Nikhil


---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 5, 2026 at 9:06 AM PT
Subject: Re: Exec update: Hosted overload protection (circuit breakers + load shedding) — canary results + rollout plan

Aligned on the Hosted rollout.

Dedicated check: can you confirm none of the new breaker logic is evaluated on Dedicated pools by default (i.e., Hosted breaker state cannot trip Dedicated routing)? We should keep semantics consistent (429/503 mapping, Retry-After), but avoid any coupling that could be interpreted as reducing reserved capacity.

Also: if we do see 503s in a region during a shared cloud incident, I’d like us to be explicit in comms whether Dedicated is impacted vs Hosted-only.

Lauren


---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 5, 2026 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Exec update: Hosted overload protection (circuit breakers + load shedding) — canary results + rollout plan

Great points.

- Dedicated: confirmed — Hosted breaker evaluation is scoped to Hosted routing keys (model/region/tier) and does not trip Dedicated pools. Dedicated keeps its existing autoscaling + admission behavior; we’re only aligning the outward-facing error taxonomy/Retry-After where applicable.
- Comms: agree we need explicit language on Hosted vs Dedicated impact in any status update. Nora/Support have a template draft we can use; we’ll add a Dedicated callout line.

Nikhil: yes on the Support/CS note. Rafael + Talia are already drafting the “why you may see more 429s (and why that’s better)” blurb + retry guidance. We’ll route to you for final wording.

I’ll proceed with enabling us-west + eu-west under caps starting 1/13 barring objections.

Sean
